author: Jim Corbett
prose_text_en: Jim Corbett, a British naturalist and hunter, was known for hunting man-eating tigers and leopards, primarily to protect villagers at the government's request. He theorized that tigers turn to man-eating when injured or old, preventing them from catching natural prey. His first major hunt was the Champawat Tiger, a tigress responsible for 436 human fatalities, confirmed by the Guinness Book of World Records. Corbett discovered that the tigress's canine teeth were broken due to an old gunshot, validating his theory of injury-induced man-eating. Corbett was a conservationist who advocated against deforestation and human encroachment, eventually establishing India's first national park, initially called Hailey National Park, now known as Jim Corbett National Park.
summary_en: Jim Corbett was a renowned hunter who transformed into a dedicated naturalist and wildlife conservationist. He hunted man-eating animals only to save human lives after witnessing how injuries rendered them incapable of hunting natural prey. Beyond his hunting career, he fought against human encroachment on forests and played a pivotal role in establishing India's first national park. His legacy is honored through the Jim Corbett National Park, which serves as a testament to his commitment to wildlife preservation.
